$schema_note: Structured results for 'When Does Personality Composition Matter for Multi-Agent LLM Teams?' (COLM 2026). Numbers match the tables on https://multi-agent-llm-teams.github.io/#results.

communication_state.description: Communication state phi (fraction of exploration acts) and per-act rates under each condition, per model. rq = questions, rd = disagreements, rs = suggestions, rack = acknowledgments.

cross_domain_outcomes.description: Objective task outcomes under the low-agreeableness (low-A) condition vs baseline. Coding and research outcomes are milestone counts; bargaining outcome is agreement rate. * p<0.01.

bargaining_acceptance.description: Bargaining acceptance rates with 95% confidence intervals and mean rounds, per model and condition.

key_findings: Low agreeableness drives every model to a disagreement-dominated communication profile (phi ~= 0.93), with large effect sizes (Cohen's d from -1.17 to -12.39).

Structured coding is buffered: despite the communication shift, milestone completion is essentially unchanged for 3 of 4 models (Claude 12.1 to 12.4, d=0.06) — the code artifact filters out process degradation ('artifact-mediated buffering').

Unstructured tasks are exposed: research milestones drop by up to 66%, and bargaining agreement collapses from ~40% to <=1% under low-A across all three tested models. High-A roughly doubles agreement.
Low-A agents still negotiate (GPT-4o revises offers in 90% of runs vs 95% baseline) but call accept_offer in only 1% of runs: agreeableness acts on the final accept decision.
Only agreeableness matters: conscientiousness and openness ablations leave communication near baseline; high-A is null because RLHF-trained models are already cooperative.

A neutral paraphrase of the low-A prompt attenuates the shift and removes cross-model convergence, but a model-specific residual persists: loaded Goldberg adjectives partly measure prompt-toxicity sensitivity.
Design recommendation: deploy low agreeableness as a bounded, lead-position critic, not a team-wide trait.
